newsitem.title: USA: Transco files to expand U.S. Gulf gas line.
newsitem.headline: Transco files to expand U.S. Gulf gas line.

text.p: Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corp said Tuesday it filed for approval with Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to expand capacity of its 30-inch, 123-mile Mobile Bay lateral and extend it by approximately 77 miles to the outer continental shelf (OCS) in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico.

The proposed 30-inch, 77-mile extension will have a capacity of 600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) and will originate at Transco's Compression Station 82 in Coden, Ala., and extend to Main Pass Block 260 in the U.S. Gulf, the company said in a statement.

In addition, Transco said it proposed to build 17.5 miles of 36-inch looping and additional compression at two onshore locations to increase capacity on the existing Mobile BAy lateral from 520 mmcfd to 1,020 mmcfd.
The company has proposed that the cost of the project be rolled into its existing transportation rates.
The proposed project, targeted to be in service during the 1998-99 winter heating season, has an estimated cost of $171.5 million.

The company will hold an open season for the proposed project beginning Nov 15, and ending Dec 16, during which it will accept written nominations from shippers desiring firm transportation capacity from the proposed receipt point in the OCS to its pooling point at "Station 85."
Transco, a unit of the Williams Cos, owns and operates a 10,000-mile natural gas pipeline system that extends from the Gulf of Mexico to New York City.
